messages:
sana: Customer reported streaming responses cut off ~30s in when going through corporate proxy. They see an EOF in the client but server shows continuous output. Need a minimal curl replay + debug bundle (request-id + tcpdump). Anyone can help assemble a concise repro?

james: Can you paste the request-id and the original curl they used? Also which proxy (env var or in-path) and whether they used --no-buffer? Proxy timeouts often bite us.

sana: Request-id: r-1a2b3c4d. Original curl from customer: `curl -v \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=revlite\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\"` (they didn't add --no-buffer or proxy flags, it's via company-wide HTTP proxy).

morgan: I repro'd this locally behind corp proxy `http://corp-proxy:3128` — got disconnect at ~31s. Repro curl that shows the problem for me: ```curl -v -N --http1.1 --proxy \"http://corp-proxy:3128\" \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \ 
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \ 
  -H \"Connection: keep-alive\" \ 
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=revlite\"```

james: Nice. Two quick asks: 1) can you paste the raw curl output (with `-v`) truncated around the EOF? 2) grab the server-side trace for r-1a2b3c4d (we need the ingress->runtime logs).

morgan: Pasted small excerpts: 
```
* Connected to corp-proxy (10.0.0.5) port 3128
> GET /v1/stream?model=revlite HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
... (streaming chunks for ~30s) ...
* Received HTTP/2 stream 0 EOF
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.example left intact
curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining
```

james: That `curl: (18)` + EOF looks like upstream or proxy closing mid-stream. Ops-bot: can you attach the ingress trace for r-1a2b3c4d?

ops-bot: Attached trace: https://trace.redwood.internal/traces/r-1a2b3c4d (ingress showed backend streaming; proxy returned `502`/`504` logs at ~31s).

kevin: FWIW, corporate proxy has an idle_timeout of 30s for tunneled streams (they drop connections with no activity at TCP level). Our server was sending small keepalive chunks ~every 10s but apparently those were aggregated by HTTP/1.1 proxy and looked idle. Two mitigation options: increase chunk frequency or use SSE keepalive comment lines to force visible chunks.

sana: Can we get a minimal curl that demonstrates both approaches so support can ask customer to try? Also need any extra headers to bypass proxy buffering (if possible).

james: Minimal test 1 (increase chunk frequency) — force smaller output from server isn't always feasible, so ask customer to try `--no-buffer` and `--http1.1` (prevents client buffering) + ensure server sends a single newline heartbeat:```curl -v -N --http1.1 --proxy \"http://corp-proxy:3128\" \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \ 
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \ 
  -H \"Connection: keep-alive\" \ 
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=revlite&heartbeat=1s\"```Test 2 (SSE keepalive comment) — if server supports it, this sends `:\n` lines every 15s to keep proxies happy.

morgan: Ran test 1 locally with `&heartbeat=1s` and saw continuous chunks; proxy no longer cut the stream. Repro steps attached.

sana: Great. For support message to customer, include exact curl they can paste and a checklist of things to collect if it still fails: 1) full verbose curl (`-v`) output 2) their `HTTP_PROXY` value or proxy hostname:port 3) server `request-id` 4) tcpdump of client->proxy (pcap) 5) timestamped logs.

james: Also note: for corporate proxies that rewrite Transfer-Encoding or aggregate small chunks, recommend using HTTP/1.1 and SSE heartbeats. If customer cannot change server behaviour, suggest using a private network path (Dedicated) or configuring proxy keepalive on their side.

morgan: I'm attaching my minimal `-v` output and a short tcpdump snippet showing `FIN` from proxy at 31.2s. Happy to convert into support-ready repro bundle. :thumbsup:

sana: Awesome — please bundle the curl snippet, verbose output, tcpdump, and the trace link then drop into Zendesk ticket and cc eng-infra. I'll draft the support note. :eyes:

kevin: I'll open an infra ticket to see if we can add a server-side SSE heartbeat option by default for streaming endpoints (low-risk feature).

sana: Thanks all — moving to next steps. If anyone else hits similar reports, point to this thread and the two curl tests above. :white_check_mark:
